I testified in front of the House Rules Committee today to talk about the working families, the local hospitals, and the kids in my district that will be seriously hurt by the budget that House Republicans are jamming through Congress. We should be focusing on lowering costs and creating jobs, not putting health care for millions of Americans on the chopping block.

We were also proud to attend the VA Clinic Open House in Lancaster, where vital resources were shared — covering housing, employment, healthcare, mental health, and dental services.

A powerful reminder of the strength, sacrifice, and unity that define our community. https://t.co/zuODFjtmew

Senate Republicans just moved one step closer to cutting health care for millions while ballooning the national debt.

Their bill — which will come back to the House if it passes — will gut Medicaid and SNAP, kill millions of jobs, shutter our local hospitals, reduce American energy independence, and harm working families across CA and the country. 

Please join me in speaking out against this — it’s not too late!

Hospitals in our district aren’t immune to what has just passed in the Senate’s Budget Bill. According to the AHA, the bill would strip away funds that help keep local hospitals staffed, equipped, and open. Our communities deserve better.

More than ⅓ of Californians are at risk of losing access to free or low-cost health coverage under the Budget Bill the Senate just passed – including kids, pregnant women, seniors, and people with disabilities. 

The proposed Medicaid cuts would mean higher out-of-pocket costs for millions, leaving families stuck choosing between getting the care they need and paying for rent, groceries, or other essentials.

I submitted an amendment to the budget that would protect patients and local health care providers that rely on Medicaid to receive, and provide, health care. 

My amendment would stop this bill’s Medicaid cuts from taking effect unless the nonpartisan Congressional Budget Office CONFIRMS it won’t harm health centers or cut people off of their insurance.

After the Rules Committee rejected my amendment to protect Medicaid, I proposed blocking cuts to Medicaid and SNAP on the House floor.

Extreme Republicans in the House blocked it yet again, but I’m keep fighting for my constituents who rely on these programs to receive health care and put food on the table.

Keep making your voice heard! This bill will harm millions of Americans across the country!
Why I voted against the budget reconciliation bill that will slash support for Medicaid and local hospitals while raising our national debt by trillions: https://t.co/27ZGsrdp20

Medicare and Medicaid support Americans in every corner of our district, from Santa Clarita and Lancaster to Palmdale to the local hospitals and clinics that serve tens of thousands of patients.

I’m fighting to push back against devastating cuts to these programs, and protect the essential health care that families rely on.

I had the opportunity to tour the @PalmdaleH2O District treatment plant and take an inside look at the systems that keep our water flowing. Our region’s water infrastructure is critical, and I’m working to secure the investments needed to keep it strong, efficient, and sustainable.

Stopped by @kpthrive Antelope Valley to meet with their doctors and team. They shared the work they’re doing to support patients and families across our community.

In Congress, I’ll keep fighting to protect Medicare and Medicaid, because every family deserves access to quality, affordable healthcare. Thanks to the Kaiser team for the warm welcome and for all you do to keep the Antelope Valley healthy.

Last week, our office joined Antelope Valley Partners for Health for their monthly briefing.

They heard from Kaliah of Three Heart Connections, who shared how the first Junior Thrivers fellowship is helping AV high school students build skills to support their mental health.

Grateful to see organizations across our community working together to share knowledge, build partnerships, and strengthen support for families in the Antelope Valley.

Today I joined @rosadelauro and @SenGillibrand to introduce the FAMILY Act! Just 27% of Americans have paid family leave through their jobs, and this bill would create a national program that helps meet the needs of new parents and people with serious personal or family health issues. The FAMILY Act will benefit working parents, children, and businesses alike.

Our office joined the Palmdale Women’s Club last week to hear from AQMNI’s husband and wife duo Ethel, and Carlo, who shared how their community mural projects in the Antelope Valley engage youth, cultivate creativity, and use art to support mental health.

We’re grateful to have artists in our community who use their creativity to heal, inspire, and bring people together.

Yesterday, my team met with @ACSCAN  to discuss their advocacy on prevention, treatment, and improving quality of life for patients and survivors.

I’m committed to protecting federal science and research programs because investing in science saves lives, drives new cancer treatments, and ensures families have access to the care they need.

Thanks to partners like ACSCAN for all their work supporting patients in our district and across the country!

25,000 people in our district will pay more for health care if the majority allows ACA tax credits to expire. 

That’s why I’m pushing for the Protecting Healthcare and Lowering Costs Act — to make these tax credits permanent, protect Medicaid, and ensure families can access affordable care.

I visited the Samuel Dixon Family Health Center in Newhall to hear about the ways they will be impacted by the GOP’s harmful budget bill. I opposed the bill in July because cuts to Medicaid and the ACA could hurt local patients and clinics like this one.

Instead of continuing down this path of raising costs on working families and hurting local health centers, Congress should be working together to lower health care costs and strengthen community clinics.

I’m back in D.C. ready to work with anyone to reverse the GOP’s extreme health care cuts and pass a budget that lowers costs for American families. 

Republican leadership — who currently control the House, the Senate, and the White House — have refused to negotiate with us, so I wanted to share exactly what these health care cuts will mean for our district.

Families across our district are worried about what would happen if House Republicans fail to extend Affordable Care Act credits.

One constituent shared how changes to the ACA could threaten her children’s coverage and her adult son’s disability care.

I’ll keep fighting to protect affordable, accessible health care for every family.
